To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

factory managers are important personnel decision-makers; they see labour relations as important, and are involved in personnel management; they see the involvement of individual workers as crucial, and are committed to this style of labour relations; they are not committed to the formal institutions of labour relations; their commitment to involvement is not deep, and is not always consistent with their other views; they are not always committed to the involvement style of labour relations.
factory managers are involved in personnel decisions, see labour relations in terms of individual employee involvement, and see their role as crucial to the success of the plant.
the managers we interviewed saw the role of personnel management as being to involve workers in decision-making and to provide them with information about their jobs.

the following issues: the role of the factory manager in personnel management; his attitudes to personnel management, and to labour relations in general; his view of the role of the personnel specialist; and the extent to which his views on personnel matters are influenced by his own background and by his experience in other firms.
